model.rationale: A D+10 district, a favorable environment, incumbency, and an overwhelming financial imbalance all point the same direction, and markets price Olszewski around 95 percent despite thin attention to the race. With no polls available, the expected margin stays near twenty points but carries wide uncertainty.
model.watch: Any late outside spending against Olszewski or an unexpected deterioration in the Democratic environment could narrow the margin, though flipping the seat would require a shift far beyond anything currently visible.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.

overview:
Johnny Olszewski enters the general election as the heavy favorite in a Maryland district that leans Democratic by about ten points. He has raised roughly $1.24 million and reports more than $640,000 in cash on hand, while Republican Dave Wallace has raised about $20,000 and holds only a few thousand dollars. No outside spending against the incumbent has been reported, and prediction markets give him roughly a 95 percent chance of winning.

No public polls of the general election are available, and national race raters have not weighed in, so the forecast rests on the district's partisan lean, the incumbent's financial dominance, and a favorable Democratic environment. The expected margin is around twenty points, with wide uncertainty because direct polling is absent. A Republican upset would require a dramatic shift well beyond anything now visible in the evidence.
